extracted.intended_audience: USPTO Class 705 (business method) patent examiners, examiner trainers, and Technology Center 2700 managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for training, searching, quality review, and procedural controls specific to examination of Class 705 (business method / business data processing) patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper search / Search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper search is the mainstay of the U.S. Patent system. The examiner must be trained in the art of analyzing the scope of the claims and searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers and Primary Examiners formulated standardized base search strategies for business technology aspects so that, once an examiner knows the technology and concepts in the application, the examiner can use the standardized search strategy to determine where to search in the U.S. patent system and which data files to search in Dialog and/or STN. An established search strategy advisory panel (managers and experienced examiners) is available to assist Class 705 examiners in developing a search strategy and to provide legal and procedural assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory search requirements for Class 705
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners perform a mandatory search for all applications in Class 705 to include a classified U.S. patent document search, and a text search of U.S. patent documents, foreign patent documents, and non-patent literature (NPL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPL searches include required search areas mapped/correlated to the U.S. classification system for Class 705. Example: an insurance application in class 705/4 requires searching 22 mandatory general business databases plus 3 mandatory insurance-specific databases, in addition to any other appropriate databases among the ~900 available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search core non-patent literature databases
rubrics_metrics.description: All Class 705 applications will be searched in the following databases (Class 705 core NPL databases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The white paper provides a core list (Figure NPL-1) including ABI/INFORM, Business & Industry, Business Week, Business Wire, Computer DataBase, Conference Papers Index, Dissertation Abstracts Online, Globalbase, INSPEC, Internet & Personal Computing Abstracts, McGraw-Hill Publications Online, Newspaper abstracts (e.g., NYT, WSJ), PR Newswire, PROMT, Softbase, Trade & Industry Database, Wilson applied science abstracts, World Reporter, etc. Examiners must run searches in these core NPL sources for all Class 705 cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search subject-specific databases per subclass
rubrics_metrics.description: Many databases contain significant NPL resources relevant to specific Class 705 subclasses; additional core databases are listed for subclasses and are required to be searched for cases in those subclasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For Health Care Management (subclass 2) search AMA journals, BIOSIS Previews, EMBASE, HealthSTAR, MEDLINE, SciSearch, and pharmaceutical-specific DBs if drugs/pharmaceuticals are involved. For Insurance (subclass 4) search American Banker, Insurance Periodicals Index, The Journal of Commerce, etc. Figures NPL-2 to NPL-4 list subclass-specific databases and newspapers to be searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in commercial NPL database tools (DIALOG/STN/CAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workgroup 2760, with support from the Technology Center and USPTO Academy, provides both basic and advanced training to Class 705 examiners in DIALOG and STN/CAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is taught in two parts: an orientation into how the database operates and how to establish a simple search query, followed by hands-on sessions using specific, real-world examples related to the business arts so trainees practice searching realistic situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Electronic Information Center (EIC) for commercial searches
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiners do not wish to search the commercial databases themselves, they can request a commercial database search by the Electronic Information Center (EIC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EIC is a USPTO/STIC branch supported by Technology Center 2700; staff includes professional searchers who perform searches for examiners. The EIC also collects new and interesting business information (including web sites) and distributes a daily e-mail newsletter to Class 705 examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on NPL when patent database is less valuable
rubrics_metrics.description: For rapidly emerging technologies and/or simple accounting procedures, the U.S. Patent database is of less value; the Class 705 examiner will rely on non-patent literature (NPL) to provide relevant art in these situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPL encompasses textbooks, newspaper/magazine articles, sales brochures, professional journals, conference proceedings, etc.; examiners should use NPL sources especially where patent literature is sparse or lagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical training curriculum to establish baseline knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical training is intended to provide examiners with current information and the history of various fields so every Class 705 patent examiner has the same baseline of knowledge regardless of prior training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent training areas included computer networking, computer organization and architecture, electronic payments, electronic catalogs, and computer security. Courses planned included Advanced Computer Networking, Financial Transaction (including ATM), Smart Cards, and General Accounting Procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field trips, conferences, and seminars as part of examiner development
rubrics_metrics.description: Field trips to industry and attendance at conferences/seminars are important to the examining process to give examiners first-hand knowledge of the inventive process and new technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field trips enable examiners to meet inventors, see the process through applicants' eyes, and understand effort and context. Workgroup 2760 planned business field trips (e.g., to Wall Street) and sending examiners to conferences such as the Financial Tech Conference to cover insurance, banking, and Wall Street technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain technical currency via industry partnerships and specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Workgroup 2760 will maintain technical currency for examiners and continue training efforts/partnerships with industry associations and corporate sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business practice specialists will be pursued from industry to serve as resources on common industry practices, terminology, scope and meaning, and standards in four basic areas: banking/finance, general e-commerce, insurance, and Internet infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish training needs for public comment and outside offers
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will publish the areas of training needs for public comment and outside offers to provide such training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural commitment to solicit external input and training offers to meet identified needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review of allowed Class 705 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A new second-level review of all allowed applications in Class 705 is required to ensure compliance with the mandatory search requirements, clarity and completeness of reasons for allowance, and to determine whether the scope of the claims should be reconsidered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory quality-control step applied to all allowed applications in the class to catch search/completeness issues and reconsider claim scope prior to allowance finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand Office of Patent Quality Review (OPQR) sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: The sampling size for quality review by the Office of Patent Quality Review is being substantially expanded for Class 705.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increasing the sampling size is intended to provide broader oversight and measurement of exam quality in the business methods area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise examination guidelines and training examples for computer-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examination Guidelines for Computer-Related Inventions and the relevant training examples are being revised in light of the State Street Bank and AT&T v. Excel decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines and training examples should reflect current case law affecting statutory subject matter and ensure examiners apply updated tests consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-process review after first office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform in-process reviews of applications after a first office action to identify areas for quality improvement within the business area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reviews check numerous items in the office actions with particular emphasis on the field of search of the prior art and patentability determinations under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103. Data from these reviews are compiled and provided to workgroup managers and used to determine training and prosecution improvements; several areas identified have been addressed via training by the Tech Center Quality Assurance Specialist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure quality efforts with defined measurement systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of quality initiatives depends on associated measurement systems; Workgroup 2760 has two measuring components in place to measure quality and the effectiveness of initiatives implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement components include the in-process reviews and expanded OPQR sampling; results feed back into training, supervision, and quality-improvement initiatives.
